name: Suzuka International Racing Course
layout: International Racing Course, full circuit (Japanese GP 2026)

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap circuit relation 284570 (raceway ways, © OSM contributors), Taubin-smoothed, 3 m stations; start line placed under the start gantry seen in the GSI aerial photo
sources.width: Measured from GSI seamless aerial photos (https://cyberjapandata.gsi.go.jp/xyz/seamlessphoto/, z18 ~0.5 m/px): white edge line to white edge line every 3rd station, rolling median; main straight (grid boxes) fixed at 14.3 m read off the photo, tree-shadowed part of the back straight set to 9.8 m from its neighbours. Official range 10-16 m (suzukacircuit.jp course guide)
sources.elevation: GSI 5 m DEM (DEM5A laser survey) via elevation tiles https://cyberjapandata.gsi.go.jp/xyz/dem5a_png/ (bare earth: at the crossover the bridge deck is not in the DEM, so the upper road uses its approach heights after median filtering)
sources.camber: none (5 m DEM too coarse for crossfall)
sources.trim: Medium-high downforce, flowing S-curves balanced against 130R/long straight: reference-level wing like Spa
sources.pitLimit: FIA Japanese GP event notes: pit lane speed limit 80 km/h
sources.pitLoss: Typical F1 pit-stop loss ~22-23 s at Suzuka (Pirelli/F1 strategy previews)
sources.raceLaps: 53 laps (FIA 2026 Japanese GP); not a 2026 sprint weekend

notes: Figure-8: the back straight (approach to 130R) crosses over the Degner-Hairpin section on a bridge. Turn numbering per FIA (18 turns).
